primitives.name: Descriptive Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Business description** > Write a professional company description for my LLC [insert name].
primitives.assumptions: The company operates within a defined industry with measurable revenue streams and customer base.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When descriptive clarity fails to align with regulatory or investor expectations.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's narrative coherence kernel where business identity is encoded as a probabilistic vector of service, audience, and growth trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency score across application contexts (bank, vendor, credit card)

primitives.name: Analytical Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Market analysis** > Generate a market analysis for my business in the [insert your industry].
primitives.assumptions: Industry growth and competitive landscape can be quantified via market share and gap analysis.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When market saturation or misalignment with demand occurs.

layer2.mapping: Derives from GSE's market-state transition model, encoding growth rate, risk-adjusted returns, and competitive positioning.
layer2.telemetry: Competitive gap index and projected market share

primitives.name: Operational Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Financial projections** > Create a 3-year financial projection for my LLC assuming [X in year 1 revenue], [Y% growth each year], and [Z% operating expenses].
primitives.assumptions: Revenue and expense trajectories follow deterministic or stochastic models with known variance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When projected cash flows fail to meet minimum liquidity thresholds.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's financial state machine, modeling profit/loss cycles and capital efficiency metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Net present value (NPV) and internal rate of return (IRR)

primitives.name: Regulatory Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Compliance & fundability** > Write a section for my business plan that highlights compliance factors banks look for: real business address, correct NAICS code, EIN, business bank account, and tradelines.
primitives.assumptions: All regulatory identifiers are verifiable and consistent with institutional data schemas.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When regulatory mismatch leads to funding denial or audit risk.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI’s compliance validation layer, where regulatory metadata is mapped to trust scores and risk profiles.
layer2.telemetry: Regulatory compliance score and audit readiness index

reasoning_traces.think:
These four primitives form a coherent system for generating funding-ready business documentation by structuring information through descriptive, analytical, operational, and regulatory lenses. Each primitive maps to a distinct but interdependent domain—identity, market position, financial health, and compliance—that collectively define a firm’s readiness for institutional funding. The universal lens integrates these domains into a single probabilistic framework, enabling GSI to perform Bayesian inference on funding likelihood. The GSE component models how changes in one domain propagate through others, creating a dynamic state space of business evolution. Failure modes include narrative inconsistency, market misalignment, financial instability, and non-compliance, all of which are detectable through telemetry signals embedded in each primitive. The epistemic trace reveals a dual structure: one rooted in empirical modeling (e.g., financial projections) and another in semantic alignment (e.g., business description). This duality reflects the tension between objective performance metrics and subjective narrative framing—a core challenge in funding narratives.
